title: Joiner edits relationship details and gets an unexplained failure
preconditions: A created the space; B joined as the partner.
B opens Account and chooses Edit relationship.
B changes the anniversary date and saves.

actions.note: B opens Edit relationship and saves a new date.

expected_behavior: A non-creator is either not offered the edit action or told plainly that only the creator can change space details.
A failed save explains the rule and preserves the current values.
The UI never implies that the partner's change was saved.
candidate_failure_modes: The partner taps a working-looking Edit relationship row, fills the form, and receives only "Unable to save. Please try again."
The partner retries because the message implies a transient network problem.
The partner believes the anniversary date changed when the server rejected it.

observed_code_behavior: Spaces enforce one active membership per user and one active partner per space at the storage layer.
Joining redeems an invite once; an expired or already-redeemed code is rejected, and a historical partner slot is permanently bound.
Leaving flips the caller's membership to left and keeps shared history for the remaining member.
Space hydration, foreground refresh, and mutation callbacks are scoped to the signed-in user id.
documented_requirement: A non-creator is either not offered the edit action or told plainly that only the creator can change space details.
A failed save explains the rule and preserves the current values.
The UI never implies that the partner's change was saved.
hypothetical_user_behavior: A fictional participant (Grace Tan) said: "We are auditing Aoi for things that do not need to exist. Walk through the shared-memory flow you actually used this week: the composer, the Keep button, pending rows, retry and edit, author labels, the feed and gallery, empty and failed states, and every confirmation or helper line. For each one, ask out loud: "Why does this even exist?" Then say what would break if it were removed, and what it cost you. Name the three most useless things and the one thing you would keep. Do not propose a redesign; remove."

A fictional participant (Hiro Tan) said: "Did this walk-through on Monday with a real import: 412 photos, batches of 50.

What earns its place: retry and edit, first and foremost. Batch three failed at item 37 and I needed to fix that one row and resend, not start the whole thing over. Pending rows too, but only because they show me something is still queued rather than silently lost.

Three I would remove:
1. The "all uploaded" success toast. It carries no count, so it tells me nothing I can verify. I open the log and count anyway. It cost me a full re-check the first time, and a glance every time since.
2. The author label on my own photos. I know who I am. In a grid it's one more thing to parse for zero information.
3. The empty-state helper line that reappears whenever a filter returns nothing. It's on a loop, so it's noise, not guidance.

Cost of the survivors: retry/edit costs me nothing and saves an entire re-upload. The toast costs me a verification I shouldn't need. That's the whole argument.

Keep: retry and edit. Delete the rest above and see if anyone misses them."
Grace Tan assumes: the sky is decorative and not the archive
Grace Tan assumes: photos can be found by date
Hiro Tan assumes: a pending upload is safely queued
Hiro Tan assumes: deleting a local copy does not delete the shared copy
